newsitem.title: UK: IBCA rates Bancoval BBB plus l-term, A2 s-term.
newsitem.headline: IBCA rates Bancoval BBB plus l-term, A2 s-term.

text.p: IBCA, the European credit rating agency, said on Friday it had assigned Bancoval a short-term rating of A2, a long-term of BBB plus, an individual rating of C and a legal of rating of 5.

"Bancoval is a registered credit institution in Spain which specialises in the provision of securities custody, settlement and clearing and to a lesser extent derivatives clearing," IBCA said in a statement.
IBCA said Bancoval's clients included banks, fund managers, insurance companies, international financial institutions and Spanish securities dealers and brokers. The latter remain its core clients.

"Given the nature of its principal activities, Bancoval's business is largely low-risk," the agency said. "It takes very limited credit and market risk and, hence, is principally at risk of loss through operational errors, which have been very low over the past few years."

IBCA said although it was a small institution in terms of balance sheet size, Bancoval had developed reasonably sophisticated IT and control systems that had enabled it to attract both domestic and other European customers.

"It is particularly attractive to Spain's independent broker/dealer community because of its neutrality: it does not trade in securities or derivatives on its own account, nor is it actively competing with brokerage firms by offering fund management products," IBCA said.

"The bank's main source of revenue is commissions from clearing, settlement and custodial services but profitability has been weak, mainly because of costs relating to a restructuring process (1993 -1995) which overhauled management, IT systems and controls and expanded the range of services provided."
The agency said in 1996, a more reasonable level of operating profitability was achieved; although management had adopted a conservative approach to creating provisions and accelerating costs.
"The bank is liquid and well capitalised with very strong total and tier 1 EU capital adequacy ratios," IBCA said.
